=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): alternate (leaves are attached at successive nodes along the stem, alternating sides; no paired or clustered attachment at a single node visible)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): distal (leaves are spaced along the stem with visible internodes, not clustered at the apex)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): compound (each leaf has multiple leaflets attached to a central rachis)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): odd-pinnate (each compound leaf has a terminal leaflet and pairs of lateral leaflets along the rachis)
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): 7 (each compound leaf has 3 pairs of lateral leaflets plus a terminal leaflet, totaling 7 leaflets; visible in multiple images)
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): alternate (leaflets are arranged alternately along the rachis, not in pairs)
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): entire (margins are smooth without teeth or serrations)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): lanceolate (leaflets are elongated with a broad base tapering to a pointed tip)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (tip is sharply pointed but not long-tapered)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (base is wedge-shaped, tapering to the petiolule)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (main vein runs from base to apex with lateral veins branching off at angles)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible, closely spaced, numerous (secondary veins are clearly visible and run from midrib to margin, forming a dense network)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny, glabrous (surface is smooth and glossy; no visible hairs or texture)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible trichomes on leaf surface)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petiole is short and not elongated; rachis is the primary axis)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petiole is round in cross-section; no wings or grooves visible)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (stem appears firm and slightly lignified, typical of young tree seedlings)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on stem)
    19. Stem color: dark green to brownish (stem is dark green with some brownish tones, especially near base)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (surface appears smooth without ridges or lenticels)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules visible at leaf bases)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no latex exudate visible upon inspection)
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no visible pulvinus at leaflet or leaf base; not applicable for non-Fabaceae, but none seen)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils observed)
F. Notes: Some leaflets show small holes and minor damage, likely from physical disturbance or minor herbivory; pink tag attached to stem, likely for research marking; multiple images confirm consistent morphology across angles. No clear habitat features visible beyond leaf litter and forest floor debris.
